text.p: The Vilnius bourse furthered its recent slide in lacklustre trade on Thursday, dealers said.
The LITINA A index, which tracks the infant bourse's 22 most active listings, fell by 27.62 points to 1416.83 while central market volume was only 182,000 litas.
Market leader Vilniaus Bank saw its shares fall to 1,240 litas from 1,260 litas in trade of 16,120 litas.
Birzhiu Dairy's shares rose by 4.57 percent to 4.81 litas and over 39,000 litas worth of its shares changed hands.
Birzhiu recently asked Nomura to place a $6 million international equity offering on its behalf.
Prices on Lithuania's central market rose steadily from August to October as the country recovered from a crisis in its banking sector.
Investors also switched from debt to equity as yields fell on T-bills but a recent rise in T-bill rates may be briefly reversing this trend, dealers say.
Volume on Thursday's secondary T-bill market reached almost two million litas and yields ranged from 11.56 percent to 14.92 percent.
